issues.description: import-notation url-mode early-exit silently skips violations when url() appears inside supports() or quoted strings
issues.detail: The check `/url\(/i.test(params)` returns early for any params containing `url(`, including cases like `@import "foo" supports(background: url(bar))` where the import target is a string and should be flagged. Previously the parser would have caught this. Needs tightening to inspect only the import target token.

issues.description: selector-not-notation walk filter changes case-sensitivity from prior includes(':not(') check
issues.detail: The original `selector.includes(':not(')` was case-sensitive; the new `walkRules(/:not\(/i, ...)` is case-insensitive. CSS pseudo-classes are case-insensitive per spec so this is arguably more correct, but it is a behavior change not documented in the changeset and not covered by tests. Selectors like `:NOT(.foo)` will now be processed.

issues.description: media-feature-range-notation early-exit regexes can miss exact-value violations and overmatch custom feature names
issues.detail: The `/(?:min|max)-/i` filter for `context` mode matches `min-content`/`max-content` value tokens (false positive, harmless) but also can silently skip exact-value cases like `@media (width: 1px)` under `['context']`. Similar concern for `/[<>]/` under `['prefix']`. These configurations lack tests; behavior changes silently.

issues.description: font-weight-notation HAS_NAMED set construction is redundant and weakens perf for relative-only mode
issues.detail: `fontWeightNonNumericKeywords` already unites relative+absolute keywords, so the `new Set([...nonNumeric, ...relative])` spread is redundant. Additionally, merging into a single HAS_NAMED means `font-weight: bolder` under primary='numeric' with ignoreRelative=true cannot fast-exit. Consider separate regexes or just `[...fontWeightNonNumericKeywords]`.

issues.description: keyframe-selector-notation HAS_PERCENTAGE regex anchoring is fragile and undocumented
issues.detail: HAS_KEYWORD uses `\b...\b` with `i` flag while HAS_PERCENTAGE uses `(?:^|[,\s])` because `\b` doesn't work around `%`. The asymmetry is correct but non-obvious. Additionally, the regex is built by joining PERCENTAGE_SELECTORS values without escaping, which is fragile if future entries contain regex metacharacters. Add a brief comment and escape helper.

issues.description: No regression tests added for new early-exit fast paths
issues.detail: Six rules get subtle behavior-affecting filters (case sensitivity in selector-not, regex semantics in import/media) but no tests confirm previously-flagged inputs still get flagged, nor that no-violation inputs short-circuit as intended. A small targeted test per rule would lock in the optimization and protect against future regex regressions.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this PR is a sound performance optimization adding regex-based early-exit gates to six `*-notation` rules, following an established pattern in the codebase. No P0 correctness regressions were found, but three P1 concerns require attention before merge: import-notation's `/url\(/i` check can silently skip string-import violations when url() appears in supports() or quoted strings; selector-not-notation flips from case-sensitive to case-insensitive matching; and media-feature-range-notation's filters can miss exact-value violations under untested config modes. Secondary cleanups: redundant set construction in font-weight HAS_NAMED, undocumented/fragile regex anchoring in keyframe-selector, and missing regression tests for the new fast paths.
